title: Only one of these is safe
spec: M02 · prompt-and-pray vs a schema the provider enforces
intro: The same raw order note, parsed two ways. One works until it doesn't; the other cannot emit a fifth status value. Four steps, including the two ways schema-enforced output still hands you something that isn't your object.

provenance.source: a narrated run of the six structured-output files shipped in M02 Step 2; the schema, the raw note, the call sites and the expected printed line are the module's own, the failing prompt-and-pray runs are reconstructed

foot: Run it for real: the OrderStatus model in Step 1 plus any tab from Step 2 — Force the Shape. Change the raw note and watch status refuse to invent a fifth value.

steps.title: Prompt-and-pray, run twice
narrative: Start with the version everyone writes first: no schema, just "respond in JSON like {...}" in the prompt, then json.loads on whatever comes back. Feed it the raw note the module uses — "AC-1042 went out with UPS, should land Tuesday, all good on our end".

Run one parses, and that is the trap. You get a dict, your tests go green, you ship. But status came back as "shipped-ish", which no downstream if will ever match, and the model invented a notes field nobody asked for.

Run two is the same code on the same input a day later. This time the model opens with "Here's the data:" and wraps the object in a ```json fence. json.loads throws on character zero. Toggle Before / After to see both outcomes of one unchanged program.

steps.title: Attach the schema — six call sites, one object
narrative: Now the safe path. You hand the SDK an actual schema — the OrderStatus Pydantic model, or the Zod equivalent — and the provider constrains generation so nothing outside the shape can be emitted. Not "asks nicely": constrains. No fences, no preamble, no fifth status.

The schema plugs into a different parameter in each SDK, and that is genuinely all that moves. Anthropic Python takes output_format=OrderStatus on messages.parse(). Gemini takes config.response_schema and also insists on response_mime_type="application/json". OpenAI takes text_format=OrderStatus on responses.parse().

The result reads back under three different names — parsed_output, parsed, output_parsed — and is the same validated object every time. You never wrote json.loads, never stripped a fence, never checked for a preamble.
steps.youDo: Run python structured_anthropic.py, then the Gemini and OpenAI files, on the same raw note.
steps.claudeSays: Still reasons in freeform internally, but every token it emits has to fit the schema — so status is decided among four options, not among all English.

python structured_gemini.py

after.title: THE OBJECT — same five fields out of all six

data.summary: Your order AC-1042 shipped via UPS and should arrive Tuesday.

views.text: Compare it to run 1 in the previous step. status is now provably one of processing / shipped / delivered / cancelled, and there is no sixth key. The enum is doing more work here than the JSON guarantee is — validity gets you a dict, the enum gets you a dict your if statements can trust.

steps.title: Two ways it still hands you nothing
narrative: "Guaranteed" is a guarantee about shape, not about arrival. Two things can still leave you holding something that is not an OrderStatus, and production code checks for both before it touches .status.

Refusal. If the model declines on safety grounds it returns a refusal instead of schema-conforming output. The parsed field comes back empty. Reach straight for order.status and you get an AttributeError on None — at 2am, on the one request that tripped the filter.

Truncation. If the reply hits max_tokens mid-object you get half a JSON object, which will not parse no matter how strict the schema was. This one is your fault, not the model's: give structured calls headroom, and treat an incomplete parse as a retry rather than a crash.
steps.youDo: Wrap every structured call: check the refusal / stop reason first, then check the parsed field is not None, and only then read a field.

resp.stop_reason = "refusal"
resp.parsed_output = None

steps.title: The edges you design for: enums and nullables
narrative: Strict mode has a rule that surprises people: every field is required, and objects forbid extra properties. You cannot leave a field off and hope the model omits it. So a value that might genuinely be missing has to be modelled, not ignored.

Try it on the other fixture order. AC-2088 is still processing and has no carrier yet. The schema declares carrier as a plain str with the description "Carrier name, or 'unknown' if none yet" — a sentinel. The model fills in "unknown", the field stays present, strict mode is satisfied.

The alternative is a nullable: Optional[str] in Pydantic, z.string().nullable() in Zod. Both are legal; they mean different things downstream. A sentinel is a string your code must remember to special-case; None is a type your code is forced to handle. Pick deliberately — the one thing you may not do is leave the field out.
steps.youDo: Change RAW to "AC-2088, nothing's moved yet, no label printed" and re-run any of the six files.

terminal.text: python structured_openai.py   # RAW = "AC-2088, nothing's moved yet, no label printed"
processing | Your order AC-2088 is still being prepared and hasn't shipped yet.

OrderStatus(order_id='AC-2088', status='processing', carrier='unknown',
            eta='unknown', summary="Your order AC-2088 is still being prepared…")
python structured_openai.py   # carrier: Optional[str] instead

OrderStatus(order_id='AC-2088', status='processing', carrier=None,
            eta='unknown', summary="Your order AC-2088 is still being prepared…")
python structured_openai.py   # carrier removed from the model entirely

the field is simply gone from the schema — the model never reports a carrier,
and you find out in the dashboard, not in the traceback

view.text: "Only one is safe" is not a slogan — it is the difference between step 1 and step 2 on identical input. But note what schema enforcement does not buy you. It guarantees the shape, never the truth: a model that misreads the note will hand you a beautifully typed OrderStatus with the wrong eta, and nothing in the schema will notice. And support varies — the current Anthropic tiers, structured-outputs-capable OpenAI models, the Gemini 2.5 family. Pin an older model and strict output can quietly degrade to the prose you were trying to escape.
